findings: The two 'cancel a booking' implementations enforce contradictory refund policies with no requirement documenting either: api/cancelBooking.ts (customer self-service) only refunds if hoursUntil(booking.start) > 24, while admin/cancelBooking.ts (support-staff panel) refunds unconditionally regardless of timing. This is directly exploitable: a customer cancelling 2 hours before their booking via the account page forfeits the refund, but the same cancellation performed by support staff (e.g. after the customer calls in) always refunds. Nothing in the requirements doc justifies staff having discretion to waive the 24-hour cutoff, so this reads as an unintentional divergence rather than a documented policy exception, and creates a direct incentive to route cancellations through support to bypass the refund cutoff.

The requirements doc ('When a booking is cancelled, its status becomes "cancelled" and the slot is released') says nothing about payment/refund handling at all, yet both implementations independently invented refund logic (one conditional, one unconditional) to fill that gap. Because there is no authoritative spec for refund eligibility, timing window, or amount, there is no way to determine which implementation (if either) is correct — the feature cannot be certified ready since the actual financial behavior of 'cancel a booking' is undocumented and was left to each implementer's own judgment.

Neither function checks booking.status before executing releaseSlot()/refund(), so there is no idempotency guard against a repeat invocation (double-click on Cancel, a retried network request, or a support agent cancelling a booking the customer already self-cancelled). A second call to either cancelBooking or adminCancelBooking on an already-cancelled booking will re-run refund(booking.payment), producing a duplicate refund with no state check to prevent it.

In both implementations, booking.status is set to 'cancelled' and releaseSlot() is executed unconditionally before/regardless of the refund step, with no error handling (no try/catch, no rollback, no compensating action) shown around refund(). If refund() fails or throws (e.g. payment gateway error), the booking is already marked cancelled and its slot already released — potentially claimed by another booking — leaving the customer cancelled-and-unrefunded with no recorded failure state or retry path tied to that booking.
